description: Darkstar is a student-led initiative participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, combining interests in physics, aerospace engineering, and computer science to explore the challenges of human exploration on Mars. Our focus is on developing practical, data-driven solutions to support mission planning, navigation and the safety of astronauts on the Martian surface.
summary:
Darkstar is an AI-powered Martian survival and navigation platform developed for NASA Space Apps 2026's *Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map* challenge. It combines real NASA mission data, interactive planetary exploration, terrain-aware navigation and artificial intelligence to help astronauts plan scientific expeditions across Mars.

Darkstar features an interactive map of Mars with surface imagery, 3D terrain visualization, topography and geological information. Using NASA elevation datasets and the A* pathfinding algorithm, it calculates routes based on distance, terrain gradients and estimated energy consumption.

Its Marswalk planning system allows astronauts to establish habitats, select scientific objectives, plan return journeys and estimate mission duration, oxygen consumption, power requirements and emergency reserves. Environmental information highlights potential hazards, including radiation, temperature extremes and dust.

An AI survival assistant powered by Groq interprets mission information and retrieves verified NASA research to provide evidence-backed guidance with scientific citations.

Darkstar addresses the challenge by transforming scattered scientific datasets into an accessible, integrated exploration tool. Its purpose is to support informed decisions in unfamiliar, hazardous environments, including situations where visibility is limited and reliable planning becomes essential.
details:
Project Details — Darkstar

Darkstar is an AI-powered Martian exploration, navigation and survival-planning platform developed for the NASA Space Apps 2026 challenge, Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map. Our objective was to transform scientific data collected by NASA missions into a practical, interactive system that could help astronauts explore Mars, conduct scientific investigations and make informed decisions in a hazardous environment.

How Darkstar Works

Darkstar combines planetary mapping, terrain analysis, route optimization, mission planning and artificial intelligence into one integrated application.

1. Interactive Martian Exploration

Darkstar provides an interactive map of Mars using NASA and USGS scientific datasets. Users can explore the planet through multiple visualization modes, including surface imagery, topography, geological mapping and three-dimensional terrain.

The platform uses imagery from the Viking missions and Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter's Context Camera (CTX), alongside elevation measurements from the Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA). A higher-resolution CTX digital elevation model provides more detailed terrain analysis within a selected region of Jezero Crater.

Users can navigate to prominent Martian landmarks, inspect coordinates and elevation, and explore areas of scientific interest.

2. Intelligent Terrain Navigation

Unlike conventional navigation systems, Mars has no established road network. Astronauts and exploration vehicles must navigate uneven, potentially hazardous terrain while managing limited resources.

Darkstar addresses this using the A* pathfinding algorithm, combined with numerical terrain analysis. Its navigation engine considers geographic distance, elevation changes, terrain gradients and configurable mobility constraints.

For rover exploration, Darkstar can compare the shortest-distance route against a route optimized for estimated energy consumption. This allows users to investigate trade-offs between direct travel and avoiding energy-intensive terrain.

The system also identifies unsupported terrain and communicates the limitations of available elevation data rather than assuming every route is traversable.

3. Astronaut Marswalk and Survival Planning

Darkstar includes a Marswalk planning system designed around extravehicular activities (EVAs).

Users can establish a habitat location, select a scientific destination and calculate an outbound and return journey. The mission planner estimates travel duration, elevation changes, oxygen requirements, electrical power consumption and emergency reserves.

Astronaut mobility parameters and resource budgets can be adjusted to explore different mission scenarios.

These calculations use hypothetical engineering assumptions and are intended as planning demonstrations rather than validated astronaut life-support predictions.

4. Environmental Awareness

Mars presents significant environmental challenges, including extreme temperatures, low atmospheric pressure, radiation exposure and airborne dust.

Darkstar incorporates historical scientific information from NASA missions and planetary data archives, including environmental observations and radiation research associated with Curiosity.

The application presents relevant hazards, scientific sources, geographic coverage and uncertainty. Historical observations are explicitly distinguished from real-time environmental conditions.

5. NASA-Grounded AI Survival Assistant

Darkstar integrates an AI assistant using Groq-hosted openai/gpt-oss-120b, with support for alternative language-model providers.

Rather than depending entirely on a language model's existing knowledge, Darkstar uses retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to supply relevant information from authoritative NASA and USGS scientific resources.

The assistant can explain Martian environmental hazards, discuss survival challenges, interpret scientific information and analyze available mission-planning context.

Users can attach their Explorer data, allowing the AI to reference actual route statistics, terrain information, resource estimates and environmental context. Scientific references are provided through clickable citations.

Technologies and Development Tools

Darkstar was developed using a modular software architecture:

  • Next.js, React and TypeScript: Interactive frontend, planetary maps, visualization and mission-planning interfaces.
  • Python and FastAPI: Backend APIs, terrain processing, route calculations and AI integration.
  • NumPy and rasterio: Processing numerical elevation datasets, terrain grids and geospatial information.
  • A pathfinding:* Terrain-aware route generation and optimization.
  • Groq API and GPT-OSS: AI inference and scientific question answering.
  • NASA/PDS and USGS datasets: Scientific imagery, elevation, geological mapping and environmental information.
  • Git and GitHub: Version control, project management and development collaboration.

The project was designed to work on conventional computers without requiring specialized aerospace hardware.

Creativity and Innovation

Darkstar's main innovation is the integration of multiple traditionally separate capabilities into a single exploration platform.

Instead of simply displaying a Martian map, Darkstar connects terrain information with navigation decisions, resource estimates, scientific objectives and AI-assisted explanations.

One important design consideration was the difference between the shortest route and the most resource-efficient route. A longer path around difficult terrain may consume less energy than a direct route across steep slopes.

Another consideration was exploration under limited visibility. Darkstar's underlying terrain-based navigation approach provides a foundation for planning journeys without relying exclusively on visible surface landmarks, although operational navigation would require additional positioning and hazard-detection systems.

We also prioritized scientific transparency. Darkstar identifies data sources, communicates geographic coverage and distinguishes measured observations from hypothetical calculations and uncertain information.

Intended Impact

Darkstar aims to demonstrate how planetary science, software engineering and artificial intelligence can work together to support future human exploration.

By making NASA data easier to explore and interpret, the platform can help users understand the practical challenges of operating on Mars, including terrain selection, mission logistics, environmental risks and scientific decision-making.

Although Darkstar is currently a research and educational prototype rather than a flight-qualified navigation system, its architecture demonstrates a possible foundation for more advanced planetary mission-planning tools.

Our guiding idea is that even when visibility is lost, scientific knowledge and intelligent navigation can continue to guide exploration.
